summary: The prepared base already fixes Numeric.minimumf, but reproduces the Vector.reduce max/min NaN discrepancy on a real gfx950 GPU. The exact candidate changes floating max reduction from maxnumf to maximumf and passes its regression plus independent adversarial NaN-position, signed-zero, infinity, and finite-boundary checks. This fully resolves the approved narrow defect scope, not the umbrella issue's deferred migrations.

tests.what_was_measured: Real GPU scalar extrema and vector reductions; reproduced Vector.reduce(max) returning +inf rather than propagating NaN while Numeric.minimumf propagated NaN.
Compile-tier Numeric.minimumf/maximumf coverage on the prepared base, confirming minimumf is already implemented.
Candidate's real-GPU regression for scalar propagating, scalar number-style, and vector reduction extrema semantics.
Independent real-GPU adversarial cases: NaN in every vector lane, both scalar operand orders, signed-zero permutations, infinities, and float32 finite extremes.
534 focused vector, arithmetic, IR, and GPU regression tests.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2; base failure and candidate/adversarial passes executed kernels and synchronized device output.

remaining_limitations: Validated on one gfx950 AMD Instinct MI355X only; other GPU architectures were not available.
No native rebuild was performed because candidate 697129d changes no C++ or native source.
The umbrella issue's deferred kernel migrations and broad arithmetic-style cleanup are outside the approved investigation boundary and remain unresolved by this candidate.
